newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast trade surplus doubled in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast trade surplus doubled in 1996.

text.p: Ivory Coast recorded a trade surplus of 748.4 billion CFA francs ($1.3 billion) in 1996, almost double the 393.7 billion CFA francs posted in 1995, the National Statistics Institute (INS) said.
It gave the following data, in billions CFA francs:

Over half of the total exports -- 1,229 billion CFA francs -- went to the European Union, and Ivory Coast had a trade surplus of 509.8 billion CFA francs with EU countries in 1996, up from 349.2 billion in 1995.
The INS said that the better trade surplus mostly reflected an increase in volumes exported rather than higher prices.

The quantity of cocoa exported -- Ivory Coast is the world's leading producer -- was 35 percent up on 1995, pushing the total value of exports up to 813.6 billion CFA francs, 30 percent higher than in 1995.
The value of oil exported soared 84 percent to 335.9 billion CFA francs, thanks to an increase in volume of 89 percent.
Oil is now Ivory Coast's second biggest export, in front of wood, down to 161.9 billion CFA francs in 1996 from 202.5 billion in 1995, and coffee, down to 151.8 billion from 199.2 billion in 1995.
The volume of coffee exported was up 4.2 percent in 1996 but prices on international markets dropped sharply over the course of the year.
Wood prices were also lower in 1996, and the effect of that on the trade balance was exacerbated by a nine percent decline in the volume exported.

The INS said the only significant development on the imports side was an increase of almost 100 billion CFA francs in the category "combustibles and lubricants", the result of greater imports of Nigerian crude oil for processing.

That was offset by a fall of around 100 billion CFA francs in imports of transport equipment. That reflects the purchase of an airplane for 93.7 billion CFA francs in 1995. ($1 = 585 CFA francs) -- Alan Raybould, Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
